newsitem.title: INDIA: India rupee dips on dlr demand from state-run bank.
newsitem.headline: India rupee dips on dlr demand from state-run bank.

text.p: The Indian rupee weakened on dollar demand from a large state-run bank to end at 35.71/72 per dollar on Monday against the opening 35.65/68, dealers said.
"The rupee was trading in a 35.66/68 range for some time," a dealer at a foreign bank said. "Then demand from the State Bank of India hit the market and pushed the rupee down."
The rupee traded at a high of 35.66 and a low of 35.72 to the dollar on Tuesday, dealers said.

Dealers said there was no immediate impact on the rupee-dollar rate from the U.S attack on Iraq. "There may be some reaction, with the rupee weakening a bit, as oil prices firm up, if the trouble persists," a dealer said.
"But the impact is likely to be marginal as our forex market is largely insulated from external factors," he said.
Premia on forward dollars remained steady at Monday's levels, dealers said. The premia on six-month dollars ended Tuesday at 10.50 percent annualised.
